title: Moving pigs safely between paddocks
subtitle: Working with how pigs think, not against them.
excerpt: Pigs are intelligent and curious but they move slowly and they do not understand the idea of going back through a gate they came in through. Moving pigs without stress depends on using temporary hurdles to create a corridor, letting them follow food, and never rushing. A calm move of two pigs between adjacent paddocks should take under ten minutes. A stressed move of two pigs can take an hour and result in escaped animals.
sourceNotes: RSPCA, pig welfare guidance (2023). BPEX, handling and moving pigs guidance (2015). NFU, pig housing and outdoor management.

glossaryTerms.definition: A solid or semi-solid temporary panel, typically 90 cm x 90 cm, used to create corridors, narrow runs, and loading guides when moving pigs. Pigs move away from the hurdle and into the space in front of it.

content.text: Pigs have a natural tendency to move away from pressure applied from behind and to follow the animal in front. They do not have a strong herding instinct, but they do follow each other and they follow food. A pig that is chased will turn unpredictably; a pig that is shown food and given a clear corridor will walk calmly.
Set up a corridor from the current paddock gate to the destination paddock gate using temporary
or stock panels. The corridor should be no wider than 1.5 m, so the pig does not have room to turn around.
Open the gate to the destination paddock before letting the pigs out of the current one. Pigs should be able to see and smell the new area before they commit to moving.
Put a small amount of food (a handful of meal or some fresh vegetation) at the far end of the corridor in the new paddock.
Open the paddock gate. Walk quietly to the back of the group and use a flat board or pig hurdle held at hip height to provide gentle pressure from behind.
Move slowly. Allow the pigs to set the pace. If a pig turns, use the board to block it and guide it back into the corridor without raising your voice.
Once all pigs are in the new paddock, close the gate behind them. Remove the corridor panels.
Do not shout or hit pigs. A stressed pig is unpredictable, moves faster than expected, and can knock over an adult who is not positioned correctly.
Do not try to turn a pig that has committed to going in the wrong direction by grabbing its ears or tail. Block the wrong direction with a board and let it find its own way around.
Do not move pigs in very hot weather (above 28°C). Pigs overheat quickly when active and have very limited ability to thermoregulate. Move them in the morning or evening.
